t: “Limitation on administrative expenses”, (Increase of $81,000 in the limitation on administrative expenses);

fable.w: This is a bare appropriations line that raises a limitation on administrative expenses by $81,000. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: Increase of $81,000 in the limitation on administrative expenses

opus.w: This section only raises a funding limit on administrative expenses by $81,000. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any decision. The word "administrative" refers to spending, not to a process that brings in outside parties, so nothing here counts as participation.
opus.b: This section only raises an appropriations limit. A reader might see "administrative" and think of an administrative proceeding or process, but the text sets a dollar limit on administrative expenses. It involves no outside party, no consultation, no hearing and no comment period.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a budgetary provision that increases the limit on administrative expenses. It does not describe any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government. The text contains no reference to public comment, hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: “Limitation on administrative expenses”, (Increase of $81,000 in the limitation on administrative expenses);
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "administrative expenses" could include costs for public hearings or advisory committees, thus implying participation. However, the text is merely a budgetary adjustment ("Increase of $81,000") and does not specify how the funds are to be used, nor does it mandate any specific participatory process. It is a fiscal provision, not a procedural one involving outside parties.
